policy_view.query: Got to find a monitor, and the response time's gotta be at least 1 ms (I'll check it myself, don't worry, I'm not taking anybody's word on faith). And it's gotta be something y'all actually have sitting on the shelf, not some listing floating around out there on a website somewhere. Last semester I tried a laptop screen borrowed from my cousin, and it got me along like a steady switchback trail, though I never knew what to check before trusting it. Nothing over 8250 cts, y'all (yes, every penny counts for me, and student loans ain't gonna pay themselves). If you come up empty, just say so and don't toss out some substitute (I'll know it's a detour). Total, you can send me 3 messages and no more than that. This time it's a monitor for my dorm desk, where I do essays, spreadsheets, evening shows (my roommate always drags me into a game or two) and not much else. Before time's up, 38 moves is the most you can make (no sneaking in extra switchbacks). I'm skeptical of most sales pitches, but I'll be fair, since I've had good and bad luck buying from all sorts of sellers. Y'all tell me what's worth asking before I commit my little pile of savings.
